title: The anatomy of a lead
intent: Rebuild of the 2026-09-10 cut, which Dillon rejected. The first version treated the reference frames as finished pictures that drift and cut; every one of them is actually a moment inside a process. This cut shows the process. The lead record is peeled open layer by layer until the indigo cavity is exposed and held; the path from form to inbox to report is laid out and then a torn scrap of paper falls on it and severs it; the film cuts back to the same wide shot with the break still there. Drafted for internal review. Not client work, not scheduled, not published.

supersedes.why: 11.6-15.2s at 4-5 beats is a slideshow. 6.9 of that cut's 15.2 seconds sat on one near-empty journal spread; the break at the notification - the whole point - was rendered as a gap between two dark dashes and was not legible; every caption was the same torn strip in the same place at the same size; and the paper-brain plate, the strongest asset available, was used as a static picture that never opened.

plateSource.provenance: Supplied by Dillon 2026-09-09 as visual direction. Licence NOT verified. Confirm before any use outside Momentum.
plateSource.newInThisCut: thread-circuit.png (ref-06) and engraved-engine.png (ref-08) were never frozen into plates/ by the first build, which is part of why it had so little to cut to. Copied byte-for-byte on 2026-09-10.

fillPlates._use: card stock and chip stock from the clean cream field at x 20-540, y 40-430 (measured luma std 0.017); cover B and the b8 cover
cover A - the outermost sheet over the record, cropped from the blank left page
cover C, and the torn scrap that falls across the path and breaks it - a piece of the same sheet, so the fibre matches

palette._source: sampled from the reference plates; see STYLE-CONTRACT.md section 1

accentThroughLine._rule: STYLE-CONTRACT.md section 2. Every beat pins its transform-origin on that plate's one indigo element, and the crops are chosen so that element lands in the same screen band beat to beat. The Momentum mark lands on the same band at the end.
accentThroughLine.deviation: b9, the engraving, is the one beat off the band: its indigo is a torn corner of the sheet and sits at roughly (1664,192). Forcing it to centre would have required cropping the engine out of its own frame. The reference image composes exactly this way. One beat of eleven, and the beat's copy sits bottom-left so the eye reads a clean diagonal.

accentBudget._rule: STYLE-CONTRACT.md section 1 sets 1.2-4.5% of frame area, 'more than ~5% and it stops being an accent'.
accentBudget.deviation: b1, b4 and b8 run 5.1-5.9%. All three are macro or cutaway frames where the indigo element IS the subject - the fibre strand and the exposed cavity. The contract's own source measurement for fibre-tangle.png is 4.61% at full frame, so any crop that makes the strand the subject exceeds the guide. Argued, not overlooked. b2, b5, b6 sit under the 1.2% floor because a paper node and a thread are physically small; thread-circuit.png measures 0.45% at full frame, so this is the reference's own value.

factCheck._rule: Every on-screen word is either pattern-level with no number attached, or sourced below. No client, competitor or vendor is named on screen.
factCheck.\"A lead is a payload.\": Source: 'Naming the humans requires the lead payload to survive the whole path from form to inbox to report.' Pattern-level.
factCheck.\"This is a whole one.\": Source: the Fagan reference configuration parses leads into the email body 'carrying UTM source/medium/campaign, the click id, a timestamp and a submission id.' A complete payload is a thing that exists and has been observed. Nothing on screen names the account.
factCheck.chips FORM / INBOX / REPORT: Source, verbatim: 'survive the whole path from form to inbox to report.'
factCheck.the break in the path: Source: 'The Zapier notifications that arrive in Gmail carry no lead data. They carry a link... There is nothing in the message to reconcile against a platform conversion.'
factCheck.\"The notification carries a link.\": Source, near-verbatim: 'They carry a link: open this Zap run in Zapier.' The vendor is not named on screen.
factCheck.\"Not the lead.\": Source, same passage: the notifications 'carry no lead data'.
factCheck.\"Most agencies never look.\": Source: '...precisely what the defect above breaks, and precisely what most agencies never notice is broken.' Pattern-level positioning claim, no statistic attached.
factCheck.\"Fix the pipe, not the report.\": Source: 'The fix is a Zap configuration change, not a reporting project.' Restated without naming the tool.
factCheck._notShown: The phone leg ('A click is not a call, and it carries no identity') is true and in the same note, but a second dead-end branch made the film argue two things at once. Cut deliberately. The thirteen-promises count and the 41-day unsent draft are also in the source and are deliberately NOT on screen: they are Momentum's own book, and a brand film is not the place to publish them.

card._what: House defaults. Every beat overrides position, size, tilt, alignment and type size in its own `card` block, so the line is set on the frame rather than dropped into one repeated lower-third. Fill is a positioned crop of the clean cream field of paper-brain.png; tiles are generated as two half-width crops from two rows of it.

accent.what: the indigo strand, measured on its traced path - screen (990,390)

beats._note: The texture bed used as an opener, not as a beat. Rack focus: the lens is turned in five discrete stops and the strand comes out of the tangle as focus finds it. Title lands after the focus resolves.

accent.what: the indigo paper node in the tube-and-node model - screen (1000,260)

beats._note: The craft desk: scalpel, bone folder, torn scraps. The line sits high-left because the model occupies the lower two thirds - the type is placed on the frame's own empty quarter, not in a safe-area box.

accent.what: the indigo cavity at the centre of the cutaway - screen (990,409)

peels._what: the outermost sheet - the whole record, closed
the stratum beneath it. Lifts the other way, so two lifts do not read as one repeated move
the last cover, sized to the whole indigo run from cavity to brainstem. Leaves downward, out of the bottom of the frame, and the core is exposed

beats._note: THE PEEL. Three real sheets lie on the plate at the cut and come off outside-in, 1.5s apart, each revealing what the photograph always had underneath. The cavity is exposed at 4.05s and the frame is then still for the last 2.5s - the held frame that breathes. The plate pulls back 1.14 to 1.00 across the whole dissection, so the film widens as the record opens.

accent.what: a different point on the same strand, further along its path - screen (990,424)

beats._note: Two seconds, no type. The pivot from the record to the path: the same strand, closer, found again by focus. Deliberately silent so the next beat lands cold.

accent.what: the blue thread, measured centroid of the indigo mask - screen (992,443)

beats.copy: It has to survive the whole path.
beats._note: The thread is already photographed into this sheet - it does not need drawing. What lands is the three stations, in order, 0.7s apart, each placed clear of the thread's own measured bounding box so no label sits on the accent.

accent.what: the point on the thread run where it is about to be cut - screen (990,409)

peels._what: a torn scrap of the same sheet falls across the run and severs it. This is the film's centre and in the previous cut it was invisible.

beats._note: Four seconds, no type. The scrap lands at 1.34s and the frame is then still for 2.66s. It covers 144 plate px of a thread run that is continuous in the photograph, so the break is a physical fact on screen, not an absence the viewer has to be told about.

accent.what: same pin as b5, to the pixel - screen (992,443)

peels._what: the same scrap, re-registered into this wider crop, already at rest

beats._note: Cut back to b5's exact frame with one thing changed. The strongest move available and it costs nothing: the audience already knows this shot, so it reads the break in the first quarter second.

accent.what: the same cavity the peel exposed - screen (990,390)

peels._what: a cover lands back over the cavity. The record closes on nothing.

beats._note: The peel run backwards, in one move, on the same plate. It rhymes with b3 and answers it negatively, which is the argument of the film. The cover owns the middle of the frame, so the line is set low-left where the plate is empty.

accent.what: the torn indigo corner of the engraved sheet - screen (1664,192), the one beat off the through-line band

beats._note: The engraving register: hatched line-work as the technical layer. Held at 1.6x upscale rather than cropped harder - see the cut list.

accent.what: the indigo paper cylinder, measured centroid - comes to rest at screen (990,362)

beats.copy: Fix the pipe, not the report.
beats._note: The slide, and it is the only one in the film because it is the only place the frame is motivated: the rail travels along the pencil axis line, right to left along the shaft, and stops with the indigo cylinder on the through-line point. Scale is locked at 1.0 so the move is pure translation - a copy stand, not a zoom. The line lands after the rail has stopped.

accent.what: where the mark lands. This crop measures 0.00% indigo, so the mark is the frame's only accent, as the contract requires.

beats._note: Endcard bed. Cropped to the handmade page and clear of the journal's blue triangle and its spine, so nothing competes with the mark.

endcard.markProvenance: clients/momentum-360/deliverables/2026-08-01-snow-logo-video/assets/momentum-360-logo-approved-circle.png - approved circle display derivative of the authoritative corporate mark (sha256 94D1059C...), per that deliverable's brand-provenance.md. Used unmodified: never recoloured, tinted or knocked out.
endcard.name: Momentum 360
endcard._note: Mark centre (990,400): the exact screen point the accent has occupied for the whole film. Measured: no column of this crop falls below 0.55 luma, so nothing dark sits behind the mark or the type.

motion._vocabulary: STYLE-CONTRACT.md section 5. Stepped landings, linear plate rails, hard cuts, no fades, no crossfades. Camera language is push, slide, lift and rack focus only - no swoop, no spin, no 3D card flip.

rhythm._rule: A film that cuts every 2.8s forever is a metronome.
rhythm.shape: Two openers, then a 7.2s dissection carrying three internal events and 2.5s of stillness; a 2.2s silent pivot; the path laid out in 3.4s; a 4.0s silent held frame in which one thing falls and breaks it; then four short beats, 2.4-3.4s, to the endcard. Two of the eleven beats carry no type at all, and they are consecutive around the film's centre.

cutList._rule: Dillon: if a beat does not work, cut it and say so.
cutList.hard crop on the engraving until the hat: CUT. The plates are 1672x941, so a hard magnification of fine engraving runs 2.2-2.8x upscale and the hatching mushes instead of resolving - it does the opposite of the intended effect. b9 holds at 1.6x, where the line-work is still crisp. To get the intended beat, re-source or regenerate the plates at >= 2400px wide.
cutList.exploded motor assembled part by part, g: REDUCED to the camera move. Assembling twelve parts from a single flat photograph needs each part's home position painted out with a matching paper crop and a duplicate flown in - twelve pairs of hand-registered elements, each a chance to be a pixel off, for a beat that reads in three seconds. The rail travelling the axis line and stopping on the cylinder resolves the same way for a fraction of the risk. Worth building properly if the motor becomes its own film.
cutList.the thread drawing itself along the sche: NOT NEEDED. The thread is already photographed into thread-circuit.png along its full path. Drawing an indigo band over a real indigo thread would have been a worse copy of a better original. What was missing was the break, and that is now a physical object.
cutList.the phone-call branch: CUT. True and sourced, but a second dead end made the film argue two things at once.

boundaries.creditSpend: none - every asset is a local file or a free font/library frozen locally. No Higgsfield, no API, no paid generation.
